text:
julie: Weird reproducible issue in the Go SDK starter: when jsonMode + function/tool calling hit an auth refresh the final parsed object contains the 401 error fields merged into the successful 200 payload, which then fails schema validation (additionalProperties). Minimal repro attached.

harry: That sounds nasty. Can you paste a tiny repro or logs? Which SDK version?

julie: repro (go, sdk-go v0.9.2):
```go
client := redwood.NewClient(redwood.Config{JSONMode: true})
resp, err := client.CallFunction(ctx, "orders.fetch", map[string]string{"id":"o-1"}, redwood.CallOpts{Schema: `{"type":"object","properties":{"items":{"type":"array"}},"required":["items"],"additionalProperties":false}`})
// Simulate expired token -> first attempt returns 401 body: {"error":"token_expired","hint":"refresh"}
// client refreshes and retries -> 200 body: {"items":[{"id":"x"}]}
// Observed: resp.Parsed == {"error":"token_expired","hint":"refresh","items":[{"id":"x"}]} and schema validation fails
```

ben: interesting. So the successful response ended up with leftover fields from the auth-error response. Does the raw 200 body logged by the HTTP client contain only the items array?

julie: yes, the raw 200 body is clean. The merge seems to happen inside the SDK parsing helper after the retry: it merges previous response map into the final parsed map instead of replacing it. I think the retry code reuses the same map buffer and does an in-place decode on top of it.

sky: we historically reused buffers to avoid allocations; looks like the optimization leaked into jsonMode path and interaction with schema validation (additionalProperties:false) makes it visible. Workaround for now: set JSONMode=false in the starter kit or run a defensive parse: `m := map[string]any{}; json.Unmarshal([]byte(resp.RawBody), &m)` then validate.

harry: can you confirm whether this affects streaming calls too? If we reuse a decoder or map across retries the stream reassembly path could also inherit keys.

julie: i ran a quick check: streaming chunked payloads weren't affected in my smoke, seems localized to buffered decode path used by CallFunction/CallTool.

ben: Proposed fix: stop reusing the decoded map across retry attempts (allocate a fresh container for each decode), or explicitly `map = map[:0]` semantics depending on language, then unmarshal into a fresh value before handing to the schema validator. Also add a unit that simulates 401->200 and asserts no extra keys remain.

sky: agree. Also add an e2e in the starter kit so new contributors don't hit additionalProperties failures during first-run. And check parity changes in JS/Py SDKs where similar buffer reuse could exist.

devex-bot: Issue created: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/issues/212 "jsonMode: residual 401 error fields merged into successful payload after auth retry" by julie. Labels: devex, bug, needs-triage.

harry: i'll own the Go fix. Plan: replace in-place decode in the retry path with a fresh Unmarshal target, add unit + e2e tests, and run quick scans across other SDKs for similar patterns.

julie: thanks! i'll update the starter-kit README with a short note about the workaround until the fix lands so new devs don't hit schema validation errors on first-run. :thumbsup:

sky: after the patch please coordinate with devex to remove the README workaround in the starter repo. Also, small PR note: include a microbenchmark to show allocation impact so we can justify change to folks who worry about perf.

harry: will do. tagging eng-runtime for visibility on retry buffer reuse.
